findings.location: sections/concise/04-themes.tex l.117-121 (physical p. 4, paragraph beginning 'That handing over meets the chants that deny any end')
findings.problem: The sentence 'Between them the psalm speaks of a flood that the Lord makes to dwell, which the antiphon leaves unsung' misplaces the text the Communion omits. The antiphon is the second half of Ps 28:10 and the second half of 28:11. propers/verified.md section 10 records that it omits 'Dominus diluvium inhabitare facit, et' and 'Dominus virtutem populo suo dabit;'. So the flood clause comes before the first sung half-verse, and what stands between the two sung halves is 'The Lord will give strength to his people' (tracked Challoner text, Ps 28:10: 'The Lord maketh the flood to dwell: and the Lord shall sit king for ever. The Lord will give strength to his people: the Lord will bless his people with peace.'). The expansive study states this correctly: the antiphon 'leaves out the flood and the strength' (sections/10-each-element.tex l.306-310). The concise study's own commentary also places the flood correctly, 'in the verse the antiphon cuts' (sections/concise/10-commentary.tex l.365-366). Compression has therefore introduced a false observation about an appointed text, on the pages that state the formulary's movement, and the document now contradicts itself.
findings.required_result: State the omitted text truly. The flood clause comes before 'the Lord shall sit king for ever', and the strength given to his people stands between the two sung halves. A replacement of the same length keeps the page fit, for example: 'Before them the psalm speaks of a flood that the Lord makes to dwell, which the antiphon leaves unsung.' The Propers: Themes and Movement must still end on physical page 4, with the commentary starting on page 5.

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex l.26-31 (p. 5, Jerome) and l.115-117 (p. 6, Hilary)
findings.problem: Compression widens two bounded statements. (a) Jerome 'gives the key to every such text'. The checked locus (research/scope.md section 3.6; In Dan. II on 7:13-14) is Jerome's reading of Dan 7:13-14 alone: that the Son of man's receiving is to be understood by Phil 2:6-8, which the Arians should have read piously. The expansive study keeps the extension as its own ('Read without that key, texts of receiving ...', sections/20-lamb-receives-the-kingdom.tex l.32-42). The concise study puts it in Jerome's mouth. (b) Hilary's reading is compatible 'only because he never makes the resurrection the beginning of the Sonship'. The study says 'does not make' (20 l.191-193), on the strength of Tract. in Ps. 2.33. 'Never' is a claim about all of Hilary's works, and no record checks it.
findings.required_result: Credit Jerome with what he says of Dan 7:13-14, and make the extension to other texts of receiving the commentary's own step (for example, 'expounding the verse ..., reads the Son of man's receiving ... by the Apostle's ...; the same key serves every text of receiving'). Restore 'does not make' for Hilary.

findings.location: sections/concise/90-apparatus.tex l.93-96 (Douay-Rheims entry) and l.147-148 (Haydock entry), rendered p. 12; sections/concise/04-themes.tex l.27-28 (p. 3)
findings.problem: The concise Douay apparatus no longer lets a reader find the quoted verses in the witness it names. (a) The entry gives Missal numbering for the Project Gutenberg Challoner text: '28:10-11' and '71:1'. That text ends Ps 28 at verse 10, which holds both sung half-verses, so there is no 28:11. Its 71:1 is the title 'A psalm on Solomon', and the Introit verse quoted on pp. 1 and 3 is its 71:2. The expansive References use the witness's numbering (28:1-10; 71:2, 8-11, 20), and its scope appendix discloses the difference (sections/90-apparatus.tex l.34-35). The concise study keeps neither. (b) The entry leaves out Douay loci quoted on page 2: Ps 28:1 and 88:1 (titles), Dan 7:1 and Apoc 1:9. (c) The Haydock entry drops the locus the expansive study gives, 'in its commentary on the seventieth psalm' (the record's source passage ...psalm-70-captivities-usher-chronology). (d) The themes quote 'Give to the king thy judgment, O God: and to the king's son thy justice' with a colon. The tracked Challoner 71:2, propers/verified.md l.396 and the expansive opening all read 'O God, and'.
findings.required_result: Give the Douay loci in the cited witness's numbering, as the expansive References do, or state the Challoner numbering difference in one clause of the concise scope appendix. Add the loci quoted on page 2 (Ps 28:1; 88:1; Dan 7:1; Apoc 1:9) and Ps 71:2, give Haydock's locus, and quote Ps 71:2 with the witness's comma.

findings.location: sections/concise/04-themes.tex l.81-88 (p. 4, paragraph 'Set beside the chants ...'); sections/concise/10-commentary.tex l.274-277 (p. 8)
findings.problem: One contrast is stated three times in four sentences: 'a King whose servants do not fight for him', 'a King who will not let servants strive for him', 'the King who has just said that his servants do not fight'. The commentary then states it a fourth time ('a few minutes after the King has said that his servants do not fight'). The second wording also goes slightly past Jn 18:36, which says only that his servants would strive if his kingdom were of this world. The passage reads as recapitulation rather than development, and the profile asks that each claim have one fullest home.
findings.required_result: State the servants contrast once on page 4, in the Gospel's own terms, and leave the Postcommunion's development to the commentary (or the reverse). Use any space freed to keep both themes pages substantively full.

findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex l.197-200 (p. 7, last sentence of 'A prisoner whose kingdom is everywhere')
findings.problem: 'Augustine's two loci do not make one position' can be read as saying that Augustine is inconsistent. The point, as the expansive comparison states it (sections/50-comparison.tex, last sentences of the Gospel paragraph), is the reverse: his readings of Ps 2:7 (eternal generation) and Jn 18:37 (birth from the Virgin) concern different births and fit together.
findings.required_result: Say plainly that the two readings concern two births and do not conflict, for example: 'Augustine's two loci speak of two births: he reads Ps 2:7 of the eternal generation and Jn 18:37 of the birth from the Virgin ...'.

observations.location: rendered concise study p. 2, row-3bd03395c37c5ada (Tract: Ps 88:27-28,30, historical setting)

observations.location: rendered concise study p. 2, Passage cells of row-6c43dd5e0531017f and row-7fbe70097919820b
observations.note: The generator labels the Introit's psalm 'Ps 71:1' but the single-citation elements 'Psalms 71:8,11', 'Psalms 2:8' and 'Psalms 28:10-11' in the same cell, as research review observed for the expansive appendix. This is a presentation inconsistency in tools/tpt proper-chronology annotations, carried into the concise page 2.

The v12 check holds every locus that a References Bible list names to a citation in the document. It does not hold the reverse: it does not test that quoted verses appear in the list, or that the list's loci exist in the witness's own numbering. So '28:10-11' passes against a Challoner text with no 28:11 (SYN-003). Locus agreement with the witness's versification looks like a missing criterion in the gate, not a fact about this leaf.

summary: Reviewed the concise study of the Claude 1962 leaf liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/f01-christ-the-king (synthesis.tex and sections/concise/01-90, every REVIEW_INPUTS hash matched). I rebuilt it in my own scratch area: 12 pages, SHA-256 e799cfed...2bb5, byte-identical to the author proof, references settled in two passes, and no overfull box, underfull box or undefined reference. The settled aux puts the inventory, overview and four sense markers on physical page 1, the chronology on page 2, the themes on pages 3-4 and the commentary start on page 5. I read all 12 rendered pages and compared them with the expansive study, which is unchanged since study-review iteration 1 (its 20 sealed files match). I also checked them against propers/verified.md, research/scope.md, research/interpretations.md and the tracked Challoner and NPNF texts. Every English and Latin quotation in the concise study is traced to the expansive study or the Missal text. From the concise prose alone, each reading's answer can be recovered. First reading: King by nature, he receives as man, through the passion and exaltation, the dominion he always had (one dominion by two rights). Second reading: a kingdom whose origin and means are from above, and which is therefore here in the faithful of every nation; kings serve it freely, in their office, and all at the judgment. Third reading: the kingdom handed over is the redeemed, brought to the vision of God, without end; the session begins now and is completed after the judgment. The commentary sets the witnesses side by side within each question (Hilary, Augustine and Theodoret on Ps 2:7; Chrysostom's rule; Augustine, Chrysostom and Aquinas on Jn 18:36-37; Augustine and Hilary on the subjection; Augustine and Bellarmine on the session). It brings the readings together at the Gospel, the Postcommunion and the Communion, and it reasons well beyond the thematic opening. Page-2 lookup on the rendered table: Gospel Jn 18:33-37 gives the Event row (Pilate's questioning in the praetorium at Jerusalem, Date unresolved) and the Composition row (John at Ephesus by early tradition, Disputed c. A.D. 90-100; A.D. 96-100). Alleluia Dan 7:14 gives the historical-setting row (the seventy years of servitude to Babylon, a duration, with the vision in Baltasar's first year) and the composition row (B.C. 570-536, with a pointer to the expansive appendix for the later dating). The Offertory Ps 2:8 pairs with the shared psalm rows (Occasion date unresolved; Before c. 165 B.C.). Every row pairs passage, occurrence, place and date without crossing a paragraph, and the writer's place and the recipients' are kept apart for Colossians. One blocking defect was introduced in compression: the themes misplace the Communion's omitted flood clause. Four advisories concern attribution breadth, the Douay apparatus, repetition and one ambiguous sentence. The Tract's page-2 row is the standing research advisory RES-014/STU-007(c), left as recorded. Limits: I relied on the study review for loci that the concise copies unchanged from the expansive study, and re-read at source only the places where the concise differs.
